## [3.29.0] — 2026-10-24

### Added
- **Beatmaker tools — `navig audio comp · vocal-fit · chop · doubles · drum-replace · tap-beat ·
  arrange`, `match --check`, a radio-ready vocal preset and scratch vocals from lyrics.** Comp the
  best take of every bar into one; see how far a vocal is from a beat's tempo and key and move it;
  chop a record into bar slices with a MIDI map; stack doubles that stay solid in mono; swap drum
  hits for your own samples or turn tapping into a beat; build intro, breakdown and drop versions
  in the beat's own key and tempo; check a mix against a reference (balance, width, low end); and
  hear a hook spoken or sung on the beat before anyone records it. New enhance settings
  `deplosive`, `deess` and `breath_control`.
- **Capability awareness: "can you access <machine>?" now answers from runtime state, not
  from prose.** When a message asks about reaching a machine (access/connect/read/ssh…
  or names a computer/server/device), the user turn carries a small runtime-derived
  block: configured routes (`ssh:<alias>`, a brain-link client relationship), the paired
  NAVIG OS web devices (browsers, **not executors**), the fact that reachability was
  **not probed in this turn** (the reply must say "not verified", never "offline"/"online"),
  and that reading private files on another machine needs explicit operator consent.
  Ordinary chat gets no block. The 2026-10-22 incident ("Can you read my DeepSeek
  conversations on my computer Neuron?") is pinned by
  `core/tests/agent/test_capability_awareness.py`.
- **Unified Capability Index** — one coherent view of what NAVIG can do, folding the
  Store's existing rows (plugins, modules, connectors, MCP servers, skills) into logical
  capabilities with every backend that serves them. Perplexity is the reference: the
  desktop app (CDP), the Sonar API connector and the plugin's skills now appear as ONE
  `perplexity` capability with three backends, their auth requirements (names, never
  values), CLI commands and MCP tools — instead of three unrelated rows.
  `navig store capabilities [id] [--multi|--json|--no-mcp]` inspects it from the CLI;
  `GET /api/deck/store?capabilities=1` serves the same fold to NAVIG OS (additive —
  clients that ignore the flag see the exact old payload). Discovery is adapter-only:
  no second registry, no cache to go stale, no untrusted plugin code imported to
  describe it; a reader that fails costs one backend, not the index. Connector
  discovery itself was repaired on the way — the Store showed ZERO connectors in a
  fresh process (nothing bootstrapped the classes), and connector rows carried raw
  ids instead of display names; both fixed via a manifests-only bootstrap that skips
  the vault's 5-6 s first-open cost, with the MCP bridge and capability index on the
  fast path and token refresh registering its provider config lazily.
- **Creative Mode — proactive capability intelligence (`navig creative`).** A deterministic
  layer over the registries NAVIG already ships: a rebuildable capability index
  (`data_dir()/creative/`, provenance `source|runtime`, token-ranked `navig creative index --q`),
  a reuse-first decision ladder (reuse → configure → compose → extend → create → no-op — reuse is
  checked first, so a wrapper is never generated for an existing tool; thresholds ≥5 repeats/7d,
  ≥3 failures/7d, ≥3 sequences/14d, below them is an explicit no-op), and detectors over your own
  operation history and goal state (no chat content). Proposals persist with content-addressed ids
  — dismissed/built are never re-proposed — rate-capped (≤5 open, ≤2/day), announced once through
  the existing notify dedup, and surfaced as a **Dashboard Suggestions card** (evidence, solution,
  reuse, benefit, risk, assumptions; Build/Dismiss; empty state first-class) plus the new
  `creative_proposal` notification type (deck default). The `creative_scan` monitor (default on,
  idle unless Creative Agent Mode, paced from the last scan) runs every 6 h. Building writes a
  SKILL.md through the standard skill contracts — shared `lint_skill_path` with the CLI, runtime
  parser security checks, atomic write with rollback on failure, overlap preflight — and
  **publishing** is local-only until `publish-enable` allow-lists a destination: a deterministic
  eight-check gate (allow-list · private visibility · branch · unchanged HEAD · no force · fresh
  foreign lock · credentials · secret scan) with path-scoped commits so unrelated work in the
  destination survives byte-for-byte. Surfaces: `navig creative status|index|list|show|build|
  dismiss|publish|publish-enable|publish-disable`, the Settings → Brain publishing section, and
  the `creative` agent tool (lookup/decide in both modes, propose Creative-only — verdicts are
  re-derived from the index, never model-supplied). No LLM imports under `navig/creative/`
  (guard-tested); mode changes never alter tool schemas or approvals.
- **Translate a selection in place (`POST /api/deck/translate`).** The Dock's new Translate
  feature sends the selected passage and a target language code (`en`, `fr`, `pt-BR` —
  validated, prompt-safe) and gets the translation back to write over the selection: the
  LLM seam runs the new builtin `translate/selection` prompt (faithful translation that
  preserves line breaks, numbers, units, proper nouns and code, returns only the
  translation, and treats the passage as delimited data — never as instructions), with a
  5,000-character limit stated in the error instead of a silent truncation, the client's
  `lang` hint passed on as a hint to verify (best-effort `navig_audio` detection when no
  hint arrives, never a plugin dependency), `{text, source, target, chars}` back, and
  honest failures: 400 `bad_target` / `bad_request` / `too_long`, 502
  `translate_failed` with the engine's reason, 503 `llm_required` when no AI connection
  answers.
- **Podcaster tools — `navig audio chapters · qa · level-speakers · debleed · highlights · ad-slot ·
  fix-word · sting`, plus breath, click and room-tone passes in `podcast-edit`.** Chapter an episode
  and write its show notes from its own words; check it pass/fail before publishing; bring every
  speaker to the same loudness; remove mic bleed from multi-track recordings; cut its strongest
  moments into captioned vertical clips; place a sponsor read at a natural pause, level-matched;
  re-speak one wrong word in the speaker's own voice (consent flag, clone deleted afterwards);
  and compose an exact-length intro sting. Local unless the command says `--allow-cloud`.
- **NAVIG Reflex — `navig endpoints` and `navig ask --plan/--commit`.** One typed model of every
  controllable thing (`id·type·info·status·typed capabilities[]`), projected read-through from the
  `navig home` inventory — `devices.yaml` stays the only storage, no second inventory and no YAML
  parsing in core. `navig endpoints list|show|set` emits one Answer envelope (`--json`), and `set`
  is idempotent (`changed:false` on replay). `navig ask` gains `--commit <token>` (`-c`), `--profile
  safe|fast|campaign` (`-p`) and `--json` alongside the existing `--plan`/`--execute`: plan resolves
  the target and blast radius and performs nothing; commit runs exactly once through the bound
  `navig …` command; a replay returns the stored Answer from the existing RuntimeStore
  (`runtime.db` `commit_plans`, 300 s TTL); unknown/expired tokens exit 2 with a hint. Destructive
  batches are plan-only in every profile; unknown utterances still fall through to the assistant.
  One `Answer` (schema version "1") renders to CLI, JSON, Alexa, Alice, the OpenAI-compatible
  assistant endpoint, deck and Telegram. Campaign integration is read-only: evidence is written
  inside the campaign workspace and cited with `navig tasks campaigns checkpoint --evidence` —
  `tasks.db` stays the single campaign writer. Docs: `docs/reference/reflex-unified.md`.
- **NAVIG doctor can see a plugin the daemon is missing.** A new "Runtime Plugins" section inventories every first-party source plugin against the **gateway's** Python, read as metadata — no plugin is imported to measure it, and the daemon's site-packages is located from its own process rather than from whatever interpreter ran the doctor. Each plugin reports a state (`not_installed` / `undiscoverable` / `activation_failed` / `inactive` / `healthy`), its declared entry point, both interpreters, whether its package files are present, and a repair command naming the interpreter to install into. Activation comes from the gateway log **bounded to the current boot** by `gateway.pid`; without that bound — or when gateways on different Pythons write one log — activation is reported `unknown` instead of green. The summary names what is absent (the `navig-msstore` shape: installed for the CLI, absent from the daemon), and `--json` carries every record on the row's `data`, a key that appears only where a check supplies one. Packages that declare no `navig.plugins` entry point (libraries core imports) are judged on presence alone and never called out for a load they never had.
- **One security posture switch — `navig approve level` now moves everything.**
  NAVIG had five level vocabularies for the same question: `approval.security_level`
  (high/medium/low), reflex risk (per-tool low/medium/high/destructive), reflex
  profiles (safe/fast/campaign), the agent `ApprovalPolicy`
  (yolo/confirm_destructive/confirm_all), and MCP read-only/destructive hints. New
  `navig.security.posture` is the single mapping: `high` → posture `strict`, reflex
  profile `safe`, agent approval `confirm_all`; `medium` → `balanced`, profile `fast`,
  `confirm_destructive`; `low` → `permissive`, profile `fast`,
  `confirm_destructive` (the level's shell exemption is not a blanket YOLO). Reflex
  `resolve_profile(None)` and a process-unset `get_approval_policy()` now derive from
  it, while an explicit `--profile`, an explicit `set_approval_policy`, and granular
  approval keys still win; per-action risk can never be lowered by a posture.
  `navig approve status` prints the derived systems, `navig approve level` reports what
  switched. Docs: `docs/architecture/security-posture.md`; tests:
  `core/tests/security/test_posture.py` (10).
- **`/status` now shows Telegram delivery health.** A new `📨 Delivery` line reports the
  brain's delivery mode (`webhook`/`polling`, read from `brain/telegram_mode.json`), how
  many accepted updates are still **unconfirmed** (`receipts.pending_count()` — the crash
  recovery trace), and how long ago the last outgoing message was recorded. That answers
  the 2026-10-22 question "is delivery healthy?" without reading logs; the incident's mode
  churn (a 10-minute flip) would now be visible on the card. Collectors never raise and a
  missing store renders zero. Tests: `tests/telegram/test_status_card.py` (delivery_health
  + render) and `tests/telegram/test_receipts.py` (`pending_count`).
- **The transport itself withholds a repeated long message.** A long, identical outbound
  body to the same chat inside five minutes is a retry, a loop, or a foreign test sender,
  not a new event — `TelegramChannel.send_message` now claims it through
  `navig.notify.dedupe` (keyed by chat + body hash, `sendmsg:<chat>:<sha1>`), logs
  `duplicate outbound message withheld`, and returns without calling the Bot API. Short
  messages (<120 chars) and anything answering a specific message (`reply_to_message_id`)
  or a business connection are exempt, because those repeat on purpose. This closes the
  class that produced the 2026-10-22 "☀️ Brief" flood (12 sends in 24 minutes) from any
  sender that uses the channel transport.
- Tests: `tests/gateway/test_telegram_send_dedupe.py` (5); `tests/gateway` +
  `tests/telegram` 4,374 passed.
- **Every accepted Telegram update now has a recorded terminal state.**
  `navig.telegram.receipts` writes `received → terminal (responded | failed)` rows at
  the single choke point that already wraps every inbound message
  (`TelegramChannel._run_update_with_turn`): one SQLite row per update id, chat/message
  ids, timestamps, status and failure detail. `pending()` lists updates that never
  reached a terminal state — the recovery trace after a worker crash — and a failing
  handler records `failed` before the exception is re-raised. This closes the 2026-10-22
  gap where nothing could answer "was the question processed and did the reply go out?".
  Tests: `tests/telegram/test_receipts.py` (8).
- **`navig vault login discover` — save the sign-ins you ALREADY have in your browser.**
  Lists the sites you look signed into in Chrome/Edge/Brave (read from a throwaway copy of
  the cookie database — only cookie NAMES and hosts, never values, never the live profile),
  each with a ready `navig vault login capture <site> --from-chrome` line; sites already in
  the vault are flagged and hidden unless `--all`. "Looks signed in" is a cookie-name
  heuristic, labelled as such — a hint about where to look, not a verified login.
  `capture --from-chrome` imports that sign-in without a new login (the real browser decrypts
  its own cookies for that one host); where App-Bound Encryption blocks the clone-decrypt it
  fails loudly and points at the interactive `capture`. Also: every `navig vault … --json`
  payload now goes through `ch.emit_json`, so a value longer than the terminal is wide no
  longer gets a newline wrapped into it (measured: `discover --json` piped at 80 columns
  produced unparseable JSON).
- **Video Lab — `navig video tighten · captions · reframe · beat-cut · broll · color-match ·
  recap · stabilize · export-check · lipsync`.** Cut fillers and long pauses out of picture and
  sound together (no sync drift); word-timed captions in SRT/VTT or burned in, in three styles,
  with optional AI translation; reframe 16:9 to 9:16 / 1:1 / 4:5 following whoever is speaking;
  cut a montage on a track's beat grid; find (and optionally generate) b-roll where the
  narration names something; match one shot's colour to another through a reusable `.cube` LUT;
  cut a recap from the liveliest windows; stabilise and de-flicker with the shake measured
  before and after; check any clip against a platform's spec and fix it (`--fix`, safe-area
  preview); and re-time a dubbed speaker's mouth (LatentSync on Replicate, `--allow-cloud`).

### Changed
- **Focus Modes retired — one agent mode `standard | creative` (owner decision 2026-10-20).**
  The six chat-tone modes (work · deep-focus · planning · creative · relax · sleep) are gone from
  every surface: Settings → Brain and the deck picker now offer **Agent Mode** with two choices
  (Standard = everyday help; Creative = proactive capability intelligence), Telegram `/mode` lists
  the same two and answers retired names with a "retired" notice while behaving as Standard, and
  all six stored values migrate to `standard` on load — the old tone-`creative` never becomes the
  capability Creative. Notification suppression decoupled: a new `dnd_enabled` preference carries
  do-not-disturb (migrated deep-focus/sleep users stay held; the evening DND buttons write it
  directly), and the five independent quiet-hours systems are untouched. The live agent prompt now
  carries the mode (previously only a dead legacy path did); tool schemas are byte-identical across
  modes, so switching can never widen the permission surface. Legacy reads stay graceful
  (`POST /mode` accepts a stale client's old id as `standard` + `migrated`), obsolete choices are
  removed from all seven locales (`settings.brain.mode.*` replaces `settings.brain.focus.*`).
- **Brain ownership is now an AUTHORITY, not a file on each machine.**
  `<config>/brain/lease.json` could not see a second machine with a copied config dir, so
  two Brains could each believe they owned one deployment. The record now lives in a
  Lighthouse Durable Object (`OwnershipRecord`, one per `sha256(deck.api_key)` tenant) with
  an atomic compare-and-set on the epoch, and the local file is a read-only cache. When the
  authority is configured but unreachable, singleton services **fail closed** (exit 77)
  instead of promoting themselves; a `client` role can read status but never change
  ownership; a migration writes its moved marker into the authority and cannot report
  complete unless the authority names the target at a live epoch. Deploy the edge (1.8.0)
  before relying on it — a single-machine install with no Lighthouse edge still works, and
  `navig brain status` says `authority.mode: local`.
- **`navig repo conflicts` stops simulating pairs that cannot conflict.** The cross-worktree radar ran one `git merge-tree` per pair — with 104 worktrees that is ~5,300 subprocesses, and measured runs of over 9 minutes with four sessions in the queue, so nobody could get a verdict. Pairs whose **both** sides are already ancestors of the default branch, and pairs at the same commit, are now skipped with a `note` (their verdict is still listed — `simulated` / `pruned` counts land in `--json`), and the rest run through a bounded 8-way pool. Soundness is the point of the design: squash-merged branches are *not* counted as in-default (`--is-ancestor` correctly refuses them) and neither are dirty sides (their ref is a `stash create` sha), because a false skip would hide a real conflict — four tests pin that, including a genuine collision still being reported. Honest limit, measured: when nearly every side is unmerged almost nothing is prunable, so the pool bounds each pair rather than the pair count; scoping the radar is a separate decision.
- **Pilot migration run: the last private changelog retired; two store release-notes
  indexed.** The navig-forge proposal sample (`.navig/archive/cleanup-2026-07-03/…`)
  imported as a `sample_artifact` and retired to the vault backup after its single
  true consumer (RESTORE.md) was re-pointed; `nuvopad/web-git` (13 entries) and
  `snapthos/public` (1 entry) imported and **retained** as release notes (registered
  in the spaces registry — they had `.navig/` but no id). Two defects the pilots
  exposed are fixed: release headers with a non-date suffix (`## [1.0.0] — Unreleased`,
  `## [3.38.34] — AI-Proposed Enhancement`) matched no parser family and were silently
  skipped; and the consumer scan matched the BARE basename anywhere — 49 "consumers"
  for a nested sample, 48 of which point at `core/CHANGELOG.md`. The scan is now
  path-aware (≥2-segment tails, same-directory bare names, root files unchanged) and
  skips its own source; `classify()` gained `sample_artifact` (self-declared samples
  are retirable without inheriting the release-notes shield from a semver title).

### Fixed
- **`python -m navig …` runs from a folder that contains a `navig/` directory.** A cwd
  holding a folder named `navig` (e.g. `C:\studio\navig`) made Python build a namespace
  package for the package ROOT — no `__file__`, no attributes — while every submodule still
  resolved, so the first `from navig import …` anywhere in core ended the run with
  `ImportError: cannot import name '__version__' from 'navig' (unknown location)`. That
  includes the `sys.executable -m navig` spawns NAVIG itself now uses for every CLI-shaped
  cron job, whose cwd is whatever space they run in. `navig._shadow_root.repair_root()`
  swaps the namespace root for the real package before anything reads it (`navig.main`
  calls it first), and `navig.cli` / `navig.cli._callbacks` fall back to a file-relative
  version so no single import can end a run. The console command was never affected.
- **A client disconnecting mid-connect no longer prints a full traceback that looks like a
  crash (Windows).** The accept guard keeps the listening socket alive through a `WinError 64`,
  but Python's proactor also spins off a fire-and-forget helper task that awaits the same
  accept — so the error was still left unretrieved and asyncio logged a
  `Task exception was never retrieved` traceback. On the operator's machine this was misread
  as "the daemon stopped suddenly" even though it kept serving for over half an hour after.
  The guard now retrieves that helper task's duplicate exception (`navig.platform.accept_guard`),
  so an aborted client leaves no crash-shaped noise in the log. A regression test proves the
  helper's exception is retrieved and that the fix cannot pass vacuously.
- **`navig guard status` / the doctor Repo Guard row report the hook that actually runs.**
  The state check looked at the standard `.claude/hooks/` copy before the path the settings
  wire, so a healthy guard wired to `scripts/agent-hooks/` was reported "outdated" (and the
  reverse order could have hidden a drifted running hook). The wiring is authoritative now;
  the standard copy is consulted only when nothing is wired.
- **Five retired model ids removed from the catalog and the shipped routing defaults** — the
  heartbeat was raising `[HIGH] nvidia's first catalog model → nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b
  is dead (404)` because that id was `models[0]` of the nvidia manifest (the substitution default
  every mistyped slot falls back to) *and* the default for `big_tasks` / `coding` / `summarize` /
  `research`. `navig ai models --check` now reports 5 retired ids instead of suggesting them:
  `nvidia:nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b` (404), `nvidia:moonshotai/kimi-k3` (410),
  `nvidia:mistralai/mistral-nemotron` (410, listed "alive" on 2026-09-15),
  `openrouter:deepseek/deepseek-r1` (404) and `openrouter:qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b` (404). All five
  join `RETIRED_MODELS`, every manifest and router table that named them now points at a
  probe-verified live sibling, and `model-catalog.generated.json` is regenerated. The liveness
  guard's "live example" is now `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b`, because the previous one
  is what this change retires — the same rotation that caught `meta/llama-3.1-70b-instruct`.
- **Saving two Lenses at once no longer deletes one of them.** `LensStore.save` read
  `index.json`, fetched the Lens's `@require` files, then wrote back the index it had read —
  so a Lens saved, enabled or removed by anyone else in that window vanished from the index
  (its folder stayed, orphaned). Every write to the index now holds one lock (threads and
  processes: the daemon, the CLI and the agent), and the network fetch happens before the
  lock is taken.
- **`navig mcp serve --transport stdio` keeps stdout pure JSON-RPC.** The `--only`
  catalogue note printed an info line to stdout — the channel IS the protocol in stdio
  mode, so every client's line-1 parse failed (caught by the narrow-stdio Recall test
  on the gate, 2026-10-20; the banner had landed hours earlier in the compact-surface
  work). In stdio mode the note now goes to stderr; other transports keep the console
  line.
- **`navig os open` works on Windows, and wherever launch codes cannot be minted.** The command dead-ended at `✗ Launch codes need a unix socket, which this platform does not have` — on the operator's own OS, while the NAVIG OS server was answering on the port. It now asks the server's `/health` first: with no launch code but a serving server it opens (or, with `--print-url`, prints) the **login page**, where the stored password from `navig os serve` still gets you in. Only when nothing is serving does it fail, and then with the launch error's own reason. The docstring and `--print-url` help now say which of the two URLs you get.
- **One digest card per chat per local day.** `navig.telegram.cards.send_card` already
  withheld a byte-identical card for ten minutes; a daily digest (SUMMARY kind — the
  review card) is rebuilt from live rows, so a second run the same day changes its text
  and slipped through. The review cron (`navig tasks review`, outpost job_26 on
  2026-10-22) therefore could deliver twice. SUMMARY cards now carry a per-(owner, chat,
  local day) claim in `navig.notify.dedupe`; a changed digest the same day is withheld
  and logged, while DETAIL cards (approvals, per-event notices) are not day-limited.
  Tests: `tests/telegram/test_cards_send_once.py` (7).
- **One Telegram card, one delivery.** `navig.telegram.cards.send_card` now claims a
  durable fingerprint (owning prefix + card key + chat + text hash) in
  `navig.notify.dedupe` for ten minutes and withholds a byte-identical repeat, so a
  retried scheduled run or a second brain cannot deliver the same review/approval/triage
  card twice; a changed card or another chat is a new delivery. The 2026-10-22 review
  card was sent by the daily `navig tasks review` cron between two operator messages;
  its duplicate rows were a separate, plugin-side issue (the `navig-tasks` tree is
  read-only in this repo by contract — see `docs/dev/outpost-brain-update.md`).
- **A scheduled digest card now waits for the reply it would interrupt.** On 2026-10-22
  the daily review card arrived at 08:30 while the operator's 08:29 question was still
  being answered (reply 08:32), so a scheduled message visually replaced the answer.
  The channel now marks a chat "turn in flight" for the duration of an inbound message
  (`navig/telegram/turn_state.py`, durable atomic state because the sender is a
  different process); `cards.send_card` parks a **SUMMARY** card instead of sending it
  while the turn is running, and the channel drains parked cards when the turn ends.
  DETAIL cards (approvals, per-event notices) are unaffected, a crashed-worker marker
  goes stale after 15 minutes, and the pending queue is bounded. Tests:
  `tests/telegram/test_turn_state.py` (5), `tests/telegram/test_cards_defer_during_turn.py` (3).
- **A Telegram conversation records the operator's words, not the model enrichment.**
  The reply path deliberately enriches the model-visible turn (web context, `[UI note]`,
  the formatting rules and the `EXPLORE_Q` mandate) so the cached system prompt stays
  byte-stable. That enrichment was also being persisted as the user's message in
  `ConversationHistory` and in the memory extractor: the 2026-10-22 DM stored ~1 KB of
  system instructions as the operator's question, and the next turn replayed them as if
  he had written them — which is why NAVIG answered about "injected skill instructions
  and diagnostic context". Channels now declare `metadata["raw_user_message"]`; the
  router hands it to the agent, which stores that (single use) at both history writes
  and the memory-extractor write. The model still sees the enrichment.

## [3.28.0] — 2026-10-20

### Added
- **NAVIG Debrief presentations (`navig debrief`)** — bare `navig debrief` turns the
  last work session into an interactive slide deck (`presentation.html` +
  `presentation.json`), `--plan` presents a proposal (always labeled proposed, never as
  done), `--profile board` trims to a 4–6 slide brief, `--export pdf` prints the deck,
  `--technical` appends the evidence appendix, `--presentation` renders an authored
  spec. Decks derive only from transcript facts plus an optional `story.json`; the
  scrolling report (`navig debrief build|list|open|shot`) is unchanged, the OS tile can
  build either, and `pip install "navig[debrief]"` now pulls the plugin (`core` extra).
- **`navig.tools.extract_json`** — public entry point for the LLM-output JSON
  parser plugins already needed (fenced/bare objects, trailing commas); the
  private `_extract_json` stays core-internal, and the private-import guard
  now has a supported path for plugin callers.
- **DeepSeek Search is the system search engine** — new `deepseek_search` provider for
  `web_search()` (POST `/v1/tools/search`, key in the vault under `deepseek_search/api_key`,
  alias `deepseek`), first in the `auto` keyed cascade. Every surface reports the engine that
  actually answered: `navig search --json` now prints `provider`, the agent tool output and
  Telegram's `[Web context — via …]` header carry it, and a **Search engine** section on
  NAVIG OS Settings → Personalization shows the active engine, available engines with key
  presence (booleans only — never key material), the fallback cascade, and a Test button
  (`GET/POST /api/deck/search/status|config|test`). NAVIG OS agent sessions search through the
  new `POST /api/deck/search` proxy, so core, CLI, MCP, Telegram and NAVIG OS all share ONE
  backend and ONE config key (`web.search.provider`); the proxy honors the
  `web.search.enabled` kill switch (403).
- **Distribution — the multi-project distribution workspace** ships in this tree:
  `navig distribution` (26 commands: status, plan, channels, research, content studio,
  publish prepare/approve/reject/run/record/verify/journal, maintain, schedule,
  analytics) plus the native NAVIG OS app (NAVIG OS → Distribution) backed by 37 deck
  routes. The bundled seed imports SCHEMA's 139 audited channel records with their
  verification evidence and computes eligibility **per project** across ten configured
  projects; publishing delegates platform posts to NAVIG Social and operator-led
  submissions to NAVIG's CDP.
- **Unified Environments data model (schema 1) — the contract under NAVIG OS's next
  switcher.** Manifests gain an additive, tolerant `kind` (`environment` · `area` ·
  `project` · defaulting to `space` for every legacy manifest), `projects` (stable
  Project-Manager registry ids, ordered and de-duplicated — many-to-many membership,
  never a false single parent) and `interface` (an open dict of dashboard/dock/menu
  bindings; layouts stay OS-side so Environment Packs can ship pointers later). The
  folder name never decides a role. Active Environment / Area / Project pointers run
  through the same canonical engine as the active Space (`NAVIG_ENVIRONMENT` /
  `NAVIG_AREA` / `NAVIG_PROJECT` → cache file as truth → config mirror, each
  independent and clearable), plus a bounded newest-first recent-Environments list.
  Membership itself stays on the existing `relations.parent` edge — no second storage
  engine, no registry migration (unknown registry keys provably round-trip), and
  Spaces/CLI/MCP behaviour is untouched.
- **Projects ↔ Environments membership — the Project Manager stays the one project
  database.** `GET /api/deck/projects` and `GET /api/deck/projects/{id}` now carry
  `environments: [<env ids>]` (many-to-many, layered on read from Environment
  manifests — never stored twice), and `POST /api/deck/projects/{id}/environments`
  with `{op: attach|detach, environment}` writes membership core-side-validated:
  unknown project → 404, non-Environment target / unknown project id / bad op →
  400, responses return the project's updated Environment list so clients converge
  without refetching. Core library: `environments_containing`,
  `environment_project_map`, `attach_project` / `detach_project` (idempotent;
  detaching a stale id still works for cleanup; attaching to an Area is refused —
  Areas hang off Environments via `relations.parent`).
- **Session goal: operator completion + evidence assessment** — `navig goal session
  complete <session> -e "…"` closes an active goal as the human override, recorded as
  `closed by operator: …` in the UI strip, `show --json` and `get_goal`. Completion
  evidence (model or operator) is now assessed, not just counted: substantive length,
  not a restatement of the objective, and any cited path-like artifacts must exist on
  disk (workspace-relative or absolute) — prose-only claims still pass, because a
  plausibility gate must not false-negative. GoalBar gains an accessible labelled group
  with a live phase region; `docs/reference/session-goal-interop.md` documents the
  Python↔OS goal contract (single writer, human-plane commands, CAS stays in-OS).
- **The daemon detects the language when nobody says it.** `POST /api/deck/voice/speak`
  without `lang` (and without a profile that carries one) now reads the language out of
  the text itself — the default voice, the lexicon and the on-device pack all follow the
  words, instead of whichever engine default came first. The Dock and the CLI already
  detect client-side; a raw API caller gets the same answer.

### Changed
- **MCP serves a compact routed surface by default; the full catalogue is `--profile full`.**
  `navig mcp serve` (HTTP, stdio, WebSocket) and `python -m navig.mcp_server` now register
  fifteen domain tools — `navig_fleet`, `navig_knowledge`, `navig_recall`, `navig_memory`,
  `navig_runtime`, `navig_automation`, `navig_web`, `navig_browser_debug`,
  `navig_browser_user`, `navig_connectors`, plus separate act domains `navig_memory_update`,
  `navig_runtime_action`, `navig_automation_apply`, `navig_browser_debug_act`,
  `navig_connectors_act` — each taking an `action` argument that dispatches to the existing
  handler. 79 actions map to 79 original operations; nothing is reimplemented and every
  original handler stays registered for `--profile full`. The definition payload falls from
  ~34.2k to ~10.1k tokens; the local TDQS of the new definitions is 5.00/5 and the
  tool+action selection benchmark scores 0.891 tool top-1 / 0.766 action top-1 (0.969 tool
  top-3, floors enforced by tests). Arguments are validated against the original tool's own
  schema, safety comes from the original operation (a read action inside a mixed router is
  not gated), and `--only` keeps its historical meaning: a restricted full catalogue. The
  full 155-tool matrix, per-action safety levels and migration notes are in
  `reports/quality/compact-surface.md`; `MCPProtocolHandler()` keeps its programmatic full
  default so existing integrations and tools are unaffected.
- **The hosted container serves the compact surface with remote trust and an exact pin.**
  `core/Dockerfile` (published at the root of `navig-run/core`, which directories such as
  Glama build) now installs `navig==<current release>` instead of the floating
  `navig>=3.27,<4`, so a rebuild cannot silently change the served tool surface; it runs as
  a non-root user with `/data` as the only writable state; and it starts
  `navig mcp serve --transport stdio --profile default --exposure remote`, with
  `NAVIG_MCP_EXPOSURE=remote` as a second line of defence for a platform that overrides the
  launch command. A locally trusted run overrides the CMD with `--exposure local`.
  `NAVIG_MCP_EXPOSURE` is validated at startup and an explicit `--exposure` flag wins over
  it; `tests/packaging/test_mcp_dockerfile.py` fails if the pin and `pyproject.toml`
  disagree, if the image drops the compact profile or remote exposure, or if it returns to
  a floating floor.

### Fixed
- **The brain's public path can no longer vanish silently.** One measured outage had both
  halves: with `gateway: false` in `~/.navig/daemon/config.json` (written 2026-10-19 when a
  failed config *read* fell back to defaults), every `navig service` boot started the
  Telegram worker and never a gateway — so no Lighthouse uplink, and the edge answered
  `503 offline` for every Stripe sale, the cloud Deck and edge-routed Telegram for two days
  while `navig service status` still reported the daemon running.
  - `navig service install` no longer rewrites the daemon config from defaults when the
    file cannot be **read** (a transient OS lock); it now refuses and writes nothing.
  - `navig doctor` → **Gateway** verifies *who* holds the port (a telegram worker
    answering there is a ⚠, not a ✓) and gains an **Uplink** row that asks the daemon
    whether the edge can actually reach this brain — could-not-verify stays a warning.
- **Distribution publication safety**: an already-submitted row can never reach the
  transport again, an uncertain result requires verification (or an explicit `--retry`)
  before re-posting, every status write walks the state-machine transitions (two new
  documented edges: the manual-package hop and verified-URL restoration), analytics
  events only say `published` for a confirmed URL, transport errors are redacted before
  storage, and the CLI now passes the NAVIG Social transport (social destinations used
  to fall through to BLOCKED).
- **Distribution approvals are enforceable**: `approve` writes a 30-day expiry, a new
  revoke path (service + `POST …/revoke`) withdraws a live approval, the gate's
  expired/revoked branches are live (store schema 1→2), and approval checks use a
  future-aware timestamp instead of `days_since`, which read every fresh approval as
  expired.
- **Distribution project scoping**: idempotency keys segment on the project (two
  projects' byte-identical acts are two journal rows) and by-id reads/writes refuse a
  row from another project when the caller names its project; the OS app persists the
  selected project across refresh and clears an open document on project switch.
- **Distribution attribution**: prepared publication destinations carry
  `ref=<channel slug>` + UTM (the tracked-URL builder is no longer dead code) and
  visit events posted with only a ref resolve back to their channel.
- **`recall history <file>` shows git's own history, not just transcripts' prints.**
  File histories previously listed only commits whose SHA some session's `git commit`
  output happened to print — a change merged by the land flow (no transcript ever
  printed it) was invisible, and the newest commit touching a file could be missing
  (caught by the real-world benchmark, question "file history: last commit"). History
  now merges `commits_touching` (git log over the file) with the session-linked
  commits, newest first, deduplicated by prefix; sessions, records and plan targets
  are unchanged.
- **Session goal reliability audit fixes** — the goal loop now refuses to spend a round
  on a turn that produced no assistant reply (context-overflow / silent API failures used
  to burn one round per failed call), completion is **evidence-gated** (`set_session_goal`
  must carry verified evidence — recorded on the goal, shown in the UI strip, the CLI and
  `get_goal`), overlapping stop events can no longer double-inject rounds (stop
  re-entrancy guard), `goal_changed` events are shape-validated before reaching the UI,
  and GoalBar/`/goal` command failures surface as toasts instead of silent unhandled
  rejections. Added: busy chip + completion-evidence line on the Goal strip, HANDBOOK
  blocked-resolution procedure, 30+ regression tests (persistence round-trip, pause/clear
  mid-flight, error recovery, evidence refusal).
- **One project identity, every checkout: duplicate worktree registrations are gone.**
  Discovery persisted every folder it walked into `spaces.json` *before* its duplicate
  check, so any session opened inside a git worktree appended a row under the main
  project's id (9 `navig` rows on the operator's machine) — and every id→root reader
  then answered "whichever row came first", flipping between checkouts between runs so
  migrations and scanners could read the wrong tree. The registry now enforces one id ↔
  one canonical path at the write layer (a checkout registers no row; an unrelated
  folder claiming a taken id is refused with a warning; registering the ancestor repoints
  a stray instance row), all readers resolve through the deterministic
  `canonical_row_for_id` (nested rows lose to the real `.git` checkout, order-independent),
  `resolve_project` is canonical-first, and the new `active_checkout(path, project_id)`
  answers "the checkout containing this file" explicitly — `recall migrate`'s consumer
  scan uses it (with `--root` still overriding). `repo remove` now also drops the removed
  worktree's legacy registry row (no tombstone, so the slug can register again).
  Regression-tested: multi-worktree families, order stability, refusal/repoint,
  removal, Windows casing, 6-way concurrent registration, missing checkouts.
- **Telegram button presses and enrichment cards can no longer fail invisibly.**
  The owner's live ⬇️ tap on a business-chat TikTok card (2026-10-20) died with
  zero log lines: the tap path's exception catch, the invalid-callback branch,
  the extension-gate rejection and the enrichment try/excepts in
  `business.py` all logged at DEBUG (absent from the live log) or toasted
  without logging. Arrival now logs at INFO, the rejection and invalid-branch
  log, and every catch on the TikTok/music enrichment and callback path is a
  WARNING with traceback — so "the press never arrived" and "the press died"
  are finally distinguishable.
- **Music link enrichment posts into business chats as the business account.**
  `music_actions.offer_links` was still handed the raw channel one line below
  the TikTok card — same `business_connection_id` gap, same rejected sends.
  It now goes through `BusinessSender` like its sibling.
- **`navig voice policy offline` bites without a restart.** The daemon's deck and Echo
  voice routes read `voice.policy` from the process-lifetime config snapshot, so flipping
  the privacy switch from a terminal left the running daemon sending text to Edge until
  it restarted (observed live: offline in the file, `X-Navig-Voice-Provider: edge` in the
  response). Both readers now go through `get_live` — one `stat` when nothing changed —
  and the deck's other voice settings (daily budget, paid fallback, stt model) follow the
  same read.
- **`NAVIG_WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER` actually overrides config now** — the env var was seeded as a
  *default* and then overwritten by any `web.search.provider` value in `config.yaml`, so the
  documented system-level override was silently dead the moment the config key existed.
  `get_web_config()` re-applies it after the config merge (known provider names only — `""`,
  the onboarding `skip` sentinel and typos never displace the configured engine). Precedence is
  now: CLI `--provider` (non-`auto`) > env > config > `auto`, pinned by tests.

### Security
- **`desktop_filesystem` is root-allowlisted whenever the MCP server is exposed remotely.**
  The eight-mode filesystem tool (`read`/`write`/`copy`/`move`/`delete`/`list`/`search`/
  `info`) previously accepted any absolute path the process could reach — acceptable for a
  trusted stdio server, unacceptable behind a proxy. A remote exposure (network transport
  or stdio declared `--exposure remote`) now enforces `mcp.files.roots`, and with no roots
  configured it denies **everything** (fail closed) instead of falling back to all paths.
  Enforcement is resolved-path based: `..`, symlinks, junctions and Win32
  extended-length (`\\?\`) prefixes cannot escape a root, and copy/move check the
  destination too. NAVIG's own config/vault/data/store/log directories and the Space deny
  list (`.env*`, `*credentials*`, `*.db`/`*.sqlite*`, `*.log`, `secrets.*`), plus credential
  files (`*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa*`, `.ssh`/`.aws`/`.gnupg` segments, …), are denied even
  inside an allowed root. `mcp.files.enforce` is `auto` (remote or roots configured),
  `always`, or `never` — and `never` is ignored for a remote exposure. Local stdio keeps its
  existing unrestricted behaviour unless roots are configured.
- **MCP transport exposure is authenticated and remote dangerous tools fail closed.**
  A non-loopback `navig mcp serve --transport http|websocket` bind now refuses to start
  without `--token`, and `--exposure remote` requires authentication even on a loopback
  bind. A loopback HTTP/WS listener running without a token advertises **only**
  `readOnlyHint: true`, `destructiveHint: false` tools (8 compact read domains instead of
  15; `--insecure-local` is the explicit local opt-out, refused on a non-loopback bind).
  Dangerous operations (`cdp_eval`, `navig_block_apply`, `connector_*_act`,
  `desktop_filesystem`, …) over a remote exposure — network bind, or stdio declared
  `--exposure remote` for a proxy — are denied unless the operator sets
  `navig config set mcp.remote_dangerous approve`; authentication alone no longer implies
  authorisation. Bearer comparison uses `hmac.compare_digest`, a non-loopback bind no
  longer gets a wildcard CORS origin, and the WebSocket token is generated before the
  exposure policy is decided so an auto-tokenised listener is not mistaken for an open
  one. Router actions are gated under the original operation's safety level and audited
  with `{router, action, original}` in the approval context. Programmatic
  `MCPProtocolHandler()` callers keep the previous local-trust behaviour.

## [3.27.7] — 2026-10-20

### Added
- **Legacy changelogs migrate into Recall — dry-run first, verified before anything
  retires.** `navig recall migrate <file> -p <project>` parses three real families
  (dated dev entries, archived session addenda, Keep-a-Changelog release notes) into
  content-addressed records with line-range locators. The default run writes nothing.
  `--apply` backs the file up under `vault/.migrations/` (sha256 manifest), imports it,
  then re-reads the ORIGINAL to verify digest + record ids + archived turns before
  reporting — and only `--apply --retire` can move a file, only when it is private dev
  history with zero consumers of its name. Release notes are indexed but never retired;
  `--delete-backup` is interactive and typed-path (the one irreversible step).
  Re-importing an unchanged file is a no-op (digest short-circuit).
- **SessionStart can carry a bounded Recall brief** (`recall.session_brief`, default
  off): recent user decisions, the unfinished count and the latest supersession, ≤1.5 KB,
  fail-open, private-chat records filtered — riding the existing `navig space context
  --brief` hook, so no new hook exists. `navig wire --recall` opts a new project in
  (the flag is the consent); `wire`/`init` print the index-your-history next step.
- **Recall now tracks what happened to a change, not only what was decided.** Schema v3
  adds a delivery `lifecycle` on every record (`proposed · implemented_uncommitted ·
  committed · merged · verified · deployed · failed · superseded · abandoned · unknown`) —
  a separate axis from decision status and verification, derived deterministically in
  `navig.recall.lifecycle` (git ancestor verdicts, explicit outcome events, verify results;
  zero LLM calls; an assistant claim never yields an `observed` basis). Evidence carries an
  exact `locator` (line range + file hash) for file-backed sources, and a metadata-only
  `commits` cache (subject/author/dates/branch/file names — never diffs) backs provenance
  queries. `navig recall verify` re-derives lifecycles after every run; existing banks
  upgrade in place (`v2 → v3`, old rows default to `unknown`).
- **Answer "what happened here?" from Recall: `navig recall history · trace · changes ·
  unfinished · conflicts`.** `history <file|plan|sha>` merges the sessions, commits and
  records behind one target into one timeline; `trace <sha|session>` walks the other side
  of a commit or session edge; `changes -p <project> [--refresh]` lists recent commits
  (git-observed into the metadata-only `commits` cache) joined to the sessions/records
  they explain; `unfinished -p` lists plans/tasks nothing verified yet (display-only —
  it never starts anything); `conflicts [--refresh]` runs the deterministic contradiction
  producer (opposed user verdicts on one subject; claims verification disproved) and
  lists open findings. All `--json`, all project-scoped, all zero-inference — and the
  commit-prefix lookup now uses an indexed GLOB (measured 0.01 ms vs 10.8 ms scanned at
  50k links), pinned by a latency + plan-shape benchmark in `tests/recall`.

### Changed
- **Session↔commit matching is prefix-symmetric, and agent worktrees belong to their
  project.** `navig recall sessions --commit` now matches the full id the operator typed
  in both directions (7-char id ↔ 12-char stored key and vice versa), instead of silently
  truncating everything to 7 characters. `.navig_worktrees/<slug>/…` paths (the agent
  isolation worktrees) now fold to their owning project for both project resolution and
  session file keys — they previously resolved to no project at all — which bumps
  `LINKS_VERSION` to 3 so stored links re-read once.
- **`navig recall migrate` gained `--root`, and runtime logs are never consumers.**
  `--root <folder>` scans a specific tree for file-name consumers — needed when a
  worktree and the spaces registry disagree on which folder a project id resolves to
  (duplicate-id registrations made the scan read the wrong checkout). The consumer scan
  now also prunes `.navig/history/**`: the operation log ECHOES command paths (including
  the migrated file's own) and must never block a retirement. Regression-tested both ways.

### Fixed
- **Every MCP definition now tells an agent what it returns and which sibling comes next.**
  Batch 2 of the catalogue audit closes the definition-quality gap the first batch measured
  (average 4.16/5 → **5.00/5**, 98 tools below the 4.5 target → **0**). Both catalogue-wide
  findings of the published evaluation are now zero across the whole surface: tools naming no
  sibling tool 93 → **0**, tools stating no result 72 → **0**, with no undocumented parameter
  and no non-strict schema. The routing/result facts live in one table
  (`navig/mcp/annotations.py:DESCRIPTION_HINTS`, 103 entries) and are appended idempotently,
  so authored text is never replaced; the connector `_act` generator now routes to the read
  verb the provider actually exposes (a search-only connector is never pointed at a fetch tool
  that does not exist), and `dock_*` titles say what the verb does instead of echoing the raw
  name. The 40-request tool-selection benchmark held at **0.800 top-1 / 0.950 top-3** — its
  top-3 caught a first wording that was too long and the sentence was tightened rather than
  the benchmark. New gate: `tests/quality/test_mcp_definition_target.py` fails if any
  advertised tool scores below 4.5, if a definition carries a scored contradiction, if a
  connector write routes at a sibling the catalogue does not serve, or if a hint names no
  advertised tool (the `recall_tables` dead-config trap). The committed census was also stale
  (152 tools at a revision that serves 154 — `perplexity_threads`/`perplexity_write` landed
  after it was generated); regenerated.

### Security
- **The gateway's bearer-less routes now require the admin token.** `GET /router/status`,
  `GET /router/traces`, `POST /router/detect`, `GET /llm/providers`,
  `POST /llm/providers/register|unregister`, `GET /sync`, `POST|DELETE /mesh/target` and
  `POST /mesh/discovery/scan` answered anyone — provider inventory, route traces, a
  classifier over the operator's router, an SSRF-shaped "register an LLM URL the daemon
  will call", and the two mesh routes that move where commands run. A caller survey found
  no live in-repo client sending credentials to any of them (the archived VS Code
  extension aside), so gating them breaks nothing: `navig flux` now sends the bearer via
  `gateway_request_headers()` — previously it posted without one — and the route tests
  assert the 401/503 as well as the behaviour behind it. Routes that *cannot* take header
  auth yet (the memory-review page's inline `fetch`, `/api/events`' `EventSource`) keep
  their current design and stay documented in SECURITY_CDP_AUDIT §4 F1.
- **`/install/*` refuses tunneled requests, not just non-LAN ones.** The join flow hands
  out the fleet `mesh_token` to any private/loopback peer — and a cloudflared tunnel
  terminates on this machine, so a request from the public internet presents as
  `127.0.0.1` and passed. It now also refuses on the two markers the deck's
  local-desktop bypass already trusts (`CF-Ray`, `X-Navig-Via`), which a caller cannot
  strip on the way in.

## [3.27.6] — 2026-10-19

### Added
- **Agent Monitor** (navig-agentctl 0.4.0) — see what your autonomous agents are doing: a run
  ledger for Claude Code sessions, subagents, long commands and `npm run land`, with verified
  results, honest progress (declared stages only — never a percentage or ETA), stall and
  vanished-process detection, a **Runs** tab in Control Center, a live Dock chip, and
  `navig agentctl runs|run|show|ack|hooks`. Run finished / failed / needs-you / stalled
  notifications are Deck-only by default.
- **Desktop notifications** — a new opt-in **Desktop** (Windows toast) notification channel,
  injection-safe and honest: if Windows has app notifications turned off it reports that instead
  of claiming a toast was shown.
- **Audio Lab — `navig audio delivery · clean-video · match · loop · podcast-edit · stems ·
  similar · dub · score`, plus cassette / vinyl / phone-call / voice-memo restoration presets.**
  Check and fix loudness for YouTube, Spotify, Apple Music, podcasts and broadcast (EBU R128,
  ATSC A/85); clean the dialogue of a video without touching its picture; match a reference
  track's tone and loudness; render seamless ambience beds at any length; cut fillers, long
  pauses and repeated words from a podcast from a cut list you review first (transcribed
  locally); split a song into stems once and remix it locally (karaoke, acapella, drumless…);
  find sounds that sound alike in a folder; dub a recording or video into other languages in
  the same voices with the timing kept; and compose music whose sections turn on the video's
  cuts, ducked under its dialogue. Everything that uploads or bills needs `--allow-cloud`;
  originals are never written; generated results are labelled in their sidecars.
- **`navig audio regenerate` — make NEW audio from a recording with AI, labelled as new.**
  The counterpart to Audio Enhance (which filters and proves it is the same recording):
  `--op voice` re-speaks speech in another ElevenLabs voice with the same words and timing;
  `--op variations` makes 1–4 new takes of a sound or cue at the source's length from a
  description (measured locally; `--describe-with-ai` also lets Gemini listen — it uploads the
  clip) plus your `--direction`, sending only text to ElevenLabs; `--op replace --stem …`
  splits the mix and either re-voices the vocals or generates a new drums/bass/other stem at
  the measured tempo, loudness-matched and remixed. Every run that uploads or bills needs
  `--allow-cloud`; `--dry-run` shows exactly what would be sent and billed. Outputs are new
  `*.regen-*.wav` files with a provenance sidecar and a "how close to the original" reading
  (informative, never a pass). NAVIG Desktop: Studio → Enhance → **New versions with AI**, with a
  "What is sent?" preview and a per-run consent box; `/api/deck/media/{id}/regenerate` runs it
  as a job whose takes become new variants beside the source.
- **Move a whole brain between machines: `navig backup export|import --brain`.** The
  config backup now carries the state a brain *runs on* — SQLite databases with their
  WAL/SHM sidecars, memory, sessions, the cron jobs, the agent workspace
  (`workspace/SOUL.md`, …), approvals, `.env` (which gates who may talk to the bot),
  license and `daemon/config.json` — so relocating the brain is one encrypted bundle
  instead of a hand-copied list of files. It implies
  `--include-secrets` (databases cannot be redacted) and **refuses to run without
  `--encrypt`**, and `--brain --format json` is refused outright. **Both directions
  refuse while the daemon is running**, so no database is copied or restored under a
  live writer, and every exit path deletes its staging copy. The vault is deliberately excluded — its key is
  bound to the machine it was made on — and both commands say so and point at
  `navig vault backup` / `navig vault restore`, which re-wrap that key for the target.
- **`navig repo gates` now shows the whole CI fleet, and `--prs` shows one repository.**
  The default view adds the self-hosted GitHub runners (online / idle / busy / offline, with the
  free-worker count and the local service state), the Actions jobs running and queued at
  GitHub with how long each waited for a runner, the **bottleneck** (lane-starved, cpu-bound,
  io-bound with `--deep`, github-queued, or a step running past twice its usual time), a
  typical-gate-time estimate that is shown **only** when at least five comparable runs agree
  closely (otherwise `—` and why), and the month's GitHub Actions spend against
  `github.ci_budget_usd` (default $10) — hosted minutes against the included quota, the billed
  net, and what GitHub's postponed per-minute self-hosted fee would add *if it were enacted*.
  `navig repo gates --prs` lists every open PR with its `gate-result` check and fingerprint,
  the async land queue, the last landed commit and, for a PR the lander refused, why. `--no-github`
  keeps it offline. `navig doctor` gains a **CI Runners** section on a runner host: services
  running, the shared lane directory writable by both accounts, the free-space floor, and a
  warning when every local account can modify the repository.
- **Self-hosted Windows runners, a PR gate, and an asynchronous lander.** `npm run land -- --queue`
  pushes the branch, opens the PR if needed, labels it `land` and returns at once; the lander
  rebases, reuses the PR's `gate-result` only on an exact fingerprint match (tree, base, tool
  versions, workflow) or gates the candidate itself, then fast-forwards `main` (a moved main
  rejects the push and the candidate is re-validated). `scripts/runners/install.ps1` provisions
  the runners under a dedicated non-admin `navig-ci` account — preview it with `-WhatIf`.
  See `docs/dev/ci-local.md` ("Runners, tiers & lander").
- **`navig vm push <vm> <files> --to <dir>`** copies files into a VM over its own key and
  known_hosts — what the clean-machine install tier needs to put a wheel into a reverted guest.
- **Connectors are wired end to end into NAVIG Desktop, and catalog batch 1 is resolved.** Sources → Connectors now also lists **Add more services**: the catalog's verified vendor-hosted MCP servers. One click adds Atlassian, Canva, Todoist, Trello, monday.com or Airtable as a workspace MCP source and opens the vendor's sign-in. Vendors that only admit approved apps (Google Docs/Sheets/Slides, Microsoft 365, Figma, Dropbox, Box, Zoom, Asana, ClickUp, HubSpot) are shown with that reason instead of a button that would fail. **Brain MCP servers** lists the servers added in the Deck, and **Use here** gives this workspace's agent the same server; a server whose config carries private headers is refused rather than copied out of the vault. Batch 1's 17 unresolved rows are now `verified` with each vendor's MCP address, checked against its docs and with a live probe of the address, and the new `client-approval` flag marks the gated ones. `GET /api/deck/connectors/catalog` takes `integration=` to filter. The brain bug fixed here: a server added through the Deck (saved under `mcp.servers`) never reached the brain agent's own MCP pool, which reads `agent.mcp.servers`. Those servers are now merged in, translated from the Deck's `.mcp.json` shape, and a name already configured wins. `navig connector catalog` gains a **Via** column, and at 80 columns it no longer squeezes the Name column out of the table.
- **`navig mcp serve` never runs the onboarding wizard** (carried from 3.27.4) and the container
  image now says so explicitly: `Dockerfile` sets `NAVIG_SKIP_ONBOARDING=1` and
  `NAVIG_NO_TELEMETRY=1`, so an image that resolves to an older patch cannot print a setup
  banner into the JSON-RPC stream either.
- **The package carries its registry name.** `mcp-name: io.github.navig-run/navig` is in the
  README, which is what lets the official registry prove ownership of the PyPI package — without
  it, publishing a release to the registry fails with `ownership validation failed`.
- MCP structured output, argument validation, tool titles/annotations and `initialize`
  `instructions` from 3.27.4 are unchanged.
- **`navig discord` — a Discord account manager.** List every server you are in (members, online, whether you own or administer it, and where the NAVIG bot is), read server details, channels and roles, and leave servers. With the bot added to a server you manage, list and search members, create/edit/delete channels and give or take roles, with an optional audit-log reason. Two identities: the official bot (`navig discord bot set`, `bot invite`) and, as an explicit opt-in behind a Terms-of-Service warning, your own account (`navig discord login`), which only reads and leaves your own servers. `navig discord join <invite>` previews an invite and opens it in your browser; NAVIG never joins by API. Every list command has `--json`.
- **The NAVIG Discord bot.** `navig discord setup` stores the bot token in the vault, installs the optional `discord.py`, turns on the Server Members intent, sets who owns the bot and opens the invite link; the daemon then runs the bot. Server admins moderate from inside Discord with `/kick`, `/ban`, `/unban`, `/timeout`, `/untimeout` and `/role add|remove|create|delete`, and the bot's owners talk to NAVIG with `/navig`. The same actions exist in the CLI (`navig discord mod …`, `navig discord role create|edit|delete`), plus `navig discord bot profile` (name, avatar, About Me), `navig discord settings` and `navig discord mod log`. Security is fail-closed: the agent answers only `discord.owners` (empty = nobody), every action needs the Discord permission and a higher role than the target (for the member and the bot), roles can't be given permissions their creator lacks, destructive actions need a confirm button only the asker can press, members are rate-limited, and every action is written to the server's audit log and NAVIG's own log.
- **Discord in the deck and NAVIG Desktop.** New `/api/deck/discord/*` routes
  (`navig/gateway/deck/routes/discord.py`) expose the `navig discord` engine to the UIs:
  status, servers (with whether the bot is in each), a server's channels and roles, members
  and bans (bot only), the moderation log, and moderation writes — kick, ban, unban, timeout,
  untimeout, role add/remove/create/edit/delete, leave a server. Every write runs through
  `navig.discord.moderation`, so the deck gets the same policy check, audit-log reason and
  local modlog as the CLI and the bot's slash commands. Every mutating request must carry
  `"confirm": true` (the UI sends it only after its own confirm step); a policy refusal is a
  403 carrying the policy's sentence, a missing token is a 409 with `navig discord setup`, and
  no token ever appears in a response. The deck shows it under Settings → Discord.
- **Agents can use your own browser — `dock_*` MCP tools and `navig dock`.** With the NAVIG
  Dock's **Let AI agents use this browser** switched on, `navig mcp serve` exposes
  `dock_status`, `dock_tabs`, `dock_open`, `dock_snapshot`, `dock_text`, `dock_act` (up to 12
  validated steps per call, the side panel's own vocabulary) and `dock_release`. Calls go
  `POST /dock/call` (gateway bearer) → one persistent, token-authenticated WebSocket the Dock
  holds (`/api/deck/dock/bridge`): ~1 ms transport, ~6 ms per MCP call end to end. Agents are
  confined to the **NAVIG agents** tab group; the user's Stop cancels and pauses them; a call
  cut off by a disconnect reports `effects: "uncertain"` and is never replayed.
  `navig dock status|unpair` show and reset the pairing.
- **`dock_*` tools grow up: locators, waits, dialogs, uploads, screenshots, logs, leases.**
  A `dock_act` step targets a `[ref_N]` or a locator (`role`+`name`, `testid`, `css`,
  `has_text`, `xpath`, `nth`) — several matches fail as `ambiguous`, never a guess; new verbs
  `fill`, `wait_for` (DOM-event driven), `extract` and `upload` (the user allows it on the page);
  `alert`/`confirm`/`prompt` are answered as they open (`dialog: accept|dismiss`) so a click never
  hangs; typing into a password/card field asks the user. `dock_snapshot since=<rev>` and
  `observe: "diff"` return only what changed. New `dock_screenshot` (an MCP image),
  `dock_console` and `dock_network` (secrets in URLs redacted). Each MCP server process is a
  session that leases the tabs it acts in; tabs run in parallel; over stdio the `dock_*` tools
  run off the reader thread, so `notifications/cancelled` stops a call in the browser and a
  quick call is never stuck behind a slow one. `dock_*` results are compact JSON.
- **NAVIG Voice for the Dock — read the selection aloud.** `GET /api/deck/voice/catalog` says
  which speech engines are usable here, what they cost, which voices suit French, Russian and
  English, and which controls each really supports. `POST /api/deck/voice/speak` turns one
  sentence-bounded chunk (≤ 1,200 characters, never silently truncated) into mp3. Auto routes
  to a free engine only. A paid provider runs only when it is named in the request; it is
  never a fallback. Being deck routes, they serve the Dock over loopback and a remote client
  through Lighthouse with no new pairing.
- **Capture triage in the Deck and NAVIG Desktop.** `GET /api/deck/inbox` now carries the two
  fields triage groups by — `content_hash` (sha256[:16] of what the classifier read) and
  `url` (the captured page, from a v1 `url:` or legacy `Source:` line; history rows keep
  the hash only). The Deck's Documents stream gains a **Triage** mode and the OS Inbox a
  **Triage** tab: duplicates group by page, one header per group with its count, and a
  keyboard pass — `j/k` move · `Enter` route · `x` skip · `e` expand a group · `1–9`
  category · `Esc` — with the row itself always one click too. The grouping and key map
  live in one module, copied byte-identically between the two apps and asserted by a
  parity test.
- **Lenses can send to your NAVIG inbox — safely (`@grant navig.capture`).** A Lens that
  declares the grant gets `navig.capture(text | {content, title?, kind?, note?})`, which files a
  Capture v1 tagged with the Lens. In Chrome such a Lens runs in its own isolated user-script
  world with a per-Lens token, so the site's own JavaScript can never use the permission, and
  the capture is addressed with the page's real URL. Elsewhere (NAVIG Desktop, `navig cdp`)
  `navig.capture` is absent for now. Settings → Lenses marks these Lenses **Can send to NAVIG**.
- **`navig mcp serve` never runs the onboarding wizard.** The MCP transport writes JSON-RPC
  on stdout; a first-run wizard on a clean machine printed a 13-step banner and a telemetry
  ping *before* `initialize`, which mcp-proxy happened to buffer but a direct stdio client
  would see as a corrupted stream. `mcp` now joins `config`/`service` in the skip list, so a
  container or a client-spawned server starts straight at the handshake.
- **`navig <plugin command>` activates instead of printing homework.** An unknown command
  that a shipped plugin provides is installed (or enabled) and then re-run; non-interactive
  callers still get the copy-paste command, and `NAVIG_NO_AUTO_PLUGIN=1` / `NAVIG_AUTO_PLUGIN=1`
  override either way.
- **`initialize` now carries `instructions`**, so a client shows the model what NAVIG is for
  before it picks a tool, instead of meeting 148 names with no context.
- **MCP argument validation, tool titles, safety annotations and strict schemas** are included
  (shipped earlier in 3.27.3, restored here after a concurrent tree reset dropped them).
- **`navig pipeline` is now the hidden alias of `navig content`.** The canonical verb for the
  content-production plugin is `navig content` (`navig-content` standalone). `navig pipeline`
  keeps working — same app, verbs, flags, exit codes and `--json` stdout — but leaves
  `--help`, the published command manifest, completions and the plugin card, and prints its
  deprecation on stderr. It is hidden only while `navig content` is registered, so an install
  whose navig-pipeline predates that entry point still shows its only verb. Recorded in
  `deprecations.json`; documented in HANDBOOK §23.5.6.
- **Manage what NAVIG remembers: pin, edit, forget, and a profile summary.** Pinned
  memories ("always keep in mind") are injected into every conversation, ahead of
  query-relevant ones (max 10, approved only) — `navig memory pin|unpin <id>`.
  `navig memory edit <id> "…"` corrects a memory in place (through the secrets filter).
  `navig memory summary [--refresh]` writes a short "What NAVIG knows about you" from
  approved memories, cached until they change. Deck routes for the Personalization page:
  `GET /api/deck/memory/facts`, `PATCH|DELETE /api/deck/memory/facts/{id}`,
  `GET|POST /api/deck/memory/summary` — deck auth only. The key-fact store gains an
  additive `pinned` column (schema v2), and `kf_meta.schema_version` now records the
  migrated version instead of the version the db was created at.
- **`navig notes` — your web sticky notes on this computer** (new plugin `navig-notes`,
  `pip install "navig[notes]"`). The NAVIG Dock syncs the notes you keep on a page, a site or
  everywhere to `<data_dir>/notes.db` over `/api/deck/notes/*` (this computer only): `list`,
  `search`, `show`, `add` (it appears in the browser on the next sync), `rm`, `export`,
  `status`. Two-way, by revision — the higher one wins, deletes travel as tombstones, an older
  copy never overwrites a newer one.
- **Recall reads web notes** (`navig recall ingest --source notes`): your words as yours,
  lines quoted from the page as page captures, checkboxes as your open / done tasks; a note
  deleted in the browser is forgotten at the next ingest. Only notes the Dock was allowed to
  sync are read, and only "the agent may use them" notes may reach a model.
- **Share notes with a Space** (`navig notes share push|pull|status`). A Space folder
  carries notes as `.navig/notes/<id>.md` — frontmatter keeps the id, revision, scope,
  geometry and tags, the body travels byte for-byte, and "the newer revision wins" is the
  same rule the Dock's sync uses. Teammates get the notes with whatever already shares the
  Space; files left behind by a deleted note are reported, never deleted. Reminders stay
  personal. From `plugins/navig-notes` (`pip install "navig[notes]"`).
- **A Customizations app in NAVIG Desktop shows what the brain runs.** Seven sections, each backed
  by `/api/deck/customize/*`: an Overview with a count per area (a section that cannot be
  read says so instead of showing zero); the active formation's agents and plugin
  subagents; the brain's skills; the workspace instruction files the agent loads (SOUL,
  AGENTS, USER, TOOLS, GUARDRAILS, MEMORY, HEARTBEAT, IDENTITY), editable with a backup on
  every save and a refusal to overwrite a newer copy; hooks; every MCP server from every
  place one is declared, with live status, enable/connect controls and whether the agent
  can actually call its tools; and the agent's tools, which can be allowed or blocked. The
  `customize` module is registered in core (`navig modules`) like every other app.
- **`navig perplexity` — the Perplexity desktop app as an agent research desk.**
  The app is a Chrome shell, so it can be driven over CDP: `ask` types the question into the
  running window, waits for the composer to stop streaming (the app swaps Submit for *Stop
  response*) and for the answer text to settle, then returns the text plus its citation URLs
  — the agent spends the app's subscription instead of its own tokens. `model`/`models` read
  and switch the composer's model (a submenu entry is a gated tier and is refused by name,
  never silently substituted); `new`/`threads`/`open` work the sidebar conversations, and
  `attach` opens the app with a debug port when it is not running. It never kills the app —
  a running instance without a port comes back as "quit it once, then attach".
- Every verb takes `--json`, prints the answer alone on stdout, and exits non-zero with a
  reason **and** a hint, so an agent can call it from a shell and trust the result.
  A timeout that lands mid-answer returns `partial: true` with a warning instead of a
  fabricated "done".
- **MCP tools `perplexity_ask`, `perplexity_models`, `perplexity_model`, `perplexity_status`**
  expose the same operations to an agent with no shell; `status`/`models` are annotated
  read-only, `ask` is open-world (the question leaves the machine).
- **Personalization switches the agent actually honours.** Five style dials
  (`style.warmth|enthusiasm|emoji|headers_lists|visual` = less/default/more) add one rule
  each to the system prompt's "How to Talk" block, after the persona's tone (all-default
  adds nothing, so prompts stay byte-identical); short replies honour them too.
  `ai.web_search.mode` = auto/always/off — `off` removes search, page fetch and the
  browser even when they ride in on the research/code toolsets. `ai.fast_answers` sends
  questions the classifier rates SIMPLE to the fast model. `ai.sources.library|connectors`
  gate the user's own sources. One deck route for the OS page:
  `GET|POST /api/deck/personalization` (whitelisted, validate-all-then-write), and
  `GET /api/deck/personalization/context?q=&incognito=` so agents outside core (NAVIG Desktop
  chat) get the same style rules, custom instructions and recalled memories.
- **`search_all` — one search across everything you own.** A new agent tool asks every
  source you allow, in parallel, and returns one labelled list: connected accounts
  (`navig.connectors.connected.search_connected`), the wiki, the Cabinet (while unlocked),
  past chats and Telegram transcripts — all on this machine — plus the web on request.
  `ai.sources.library|connectors` and `ai.web_search.mode` gate it; past chats and
  transcripts are skipped while memory is off or the chat is incognito. Every source
  reports its state (answered · skipped and why · locked · timed out · failed), so "found
  nothing" and "couldn't look" are never confused. Offered on research and big-task turns.
  The vault-first "which connectors are connected" logic moved from `connector_cmd` to
  `navig/connectors/connected.py`, shared by the CLI and the tool.
- **Session goals** — a goal one NAVIG Desktop session works until done: `navig goal session
  set <session> "<objective>"` arms the session, which then injects a `<goal_round>`
  prompt each time it goes idle (Round N/max, default 12) until the agent marks the goal
  complete, reports a blocker, or spends its rounds. Add `show|list|pause|resume|clear`,
  a `goal:` config block (`enabled`, `max_rounds`, `blocked_after_rounds`, `tool_policy`),
  and `get_goal` / `set_session_goal` tools on the session. Distinct from standing goals
  (`navig goal add`): no schedule, no missions — the loop lives in the session itself.
- **`navig space context --brief` — every session starts with its neighborhood.**
  The SessionStart hook (`navig wire`'s `.claude/settings.json`) now runs the brief
  instead of a bare `space current`: active space + phase title, one `●`/`○` line per
  parent/link with file counts and unavailable reasons, a cycle warning when present,
  and a count line — capped at ten lines. It **never fails**: any reader error degrades
  to the old one-liner, because a broken relation must not break session start.
  Existing wired spaces pick the new command up on their next `navig wire` (the hook
  file is write-once by design).
- **Connected Spaces over MCP — four provider-neutral tools.** `navig_space_current`
  (identity + phase + edge counts), `navig_space_related` (the shared graph payload:
  parent/links/children/inbound, availability, cycle flag), `navig_space_context`
  (provenance-carrying linked-context snapshot with focus and limit) and
  `navig_space_read` — a single-file read behind the linked-context guard: the target
  must be the active Space or reachable through its parent/link edges, match the
  edge's include/exclude globs, pass the deny list (vault/env/credentials/sessions/
  state/databases/logs) and resolve inside the Space's own folder (junctions cannot
  escape); refusals answer with the reason and the fix, never content. Same core
  library as the CLI and the deck — one engine, so an MCP client, the deck and
  `navig space` can never disagree about what a Space may show. Safety: reads are
  `moderate` (gated), the metadata readers `safe`.
- **Cross-Space relations storage — `navig.spaces.relations`.** A Space's
  `.navig/space.json` may now carry a logical `relations` block (`parent` + `links`
  with `include`/`exclude` globs and a `profile`) and a top-level `collections`
  list for UI grouping. Metadata only: paths never move, no new folders, reads of
  a malformed block degrade to "no relations" instead of raising, unknown or
  missing targets resolve as *unavailable*, and writes refuse self-links,
  unregistered targets and parent cycles. v1 access is `read` only — the module
  writes manifests, never another Space's files. CLI verbs (`navig space link`
  and friends) and the deck endpoints follow in this same release.
- **Chat starters from your own sources.** `GET /api/deck/suggestions/starters` (cached five
  minutes, `?fresh=1` to bypass) returns up to four suggestions built from what you actually
  have — memories waiting for review (opens Settings → Personalization) and the accounts you
  connected (Gmail, Calendar, GitHub, Slack, Linear, Notion, Drive, YouTube). Pure reads, no
  network: `navig/agent/proactive/starters.py`. NAVIG Desktop shows them on the empty chat screen.
- **Lighthouse 1.7.0 — the sign-in relay.** `GET /oauth/callback` on the self-hosted edge
  302s the browser to this machine's local callback port (the same one the Cloudflare login
  uses), which is how a provider that refuses `http://` redirects — Threads — completes a
  sign-in with **no pasted URL**: the browser doing the sign-in is this machine, so no tunnel
  and no uplink hop is needed. It addresses nothing (no Bearer, no tenant, no Durable Object),
  carries `?code=…&state=…` untouched, and the state token is checked by the waiting flow.
  The shipped worker bundle ships the same version; `navig lighthouse status` reports an edge
  that lacks the route, so redeploy after upgrading.
- **`navig vault classify [--apply] [--category] [--json]`** — organise the vault: every
  item gets a name (only where it has none), a category (ai · search · social · messaging ·
  infra · payments · devtools · internal · hosts · logins · sessions · personal), the issuer
  and the website it is managed on (inferred from the value's shape, e.g. `EAA…` → Meta),
  and `duplicate-of:<other>` tags for byte-identical values. Dry-run by default; `--apply`
  writes metadata only and never overwrites an existing name, category, issuer or website.
  Values are read in memory and never printed (the Hint column shows at most 4 characters).
- **`navig vault list --category/--tag/--search`** (search matches the name, path, provider,
  issuer, website, tags and notes) with Category and Issuer columns, and
  **`navig vault edit --category/--issuer/--website/--note/--tag/--untag`** — organisation
  edits never touch the secret itself.
- **Offline neural voices route through the whole voice stack.** `TTSProvider.LOCAL`
  (sherpa-onnx + an installed Piper pack, the navig-audio `local-tts` extra) is
  catalogued honestly — available only when the extra AND at least one pack are present,
  with the two states named apart — and the `offline` policy resolves to it or refuses
  with what is missing; it never falls back to a network provider. Speech profiles may
  name `provider: local`, and the deck speak route sets its `Content-Type` from the real
  format (`audio/wav` for the on-device engine, `audio/mpeg` for the cloud ones) instead
  of declaring mp3 over every byte. Packs are installed, checksum-verified and removed
  with `navig voice packs list|install|remove` (details in navig-audio 0.6.0).
- **Voice profiles, a voice policy and a daily budget for paid speech.** Voice profiles are
  universal presets with tool `speech` (provider, model, voice, language, speed, pitch,
  ElevenLabs stability / similarity, delivery note, pronunciation rules). Six builtins:
  French narrator, Russian deep narrator, English reader, calm audiobook, news presenter,
